syllabus.topics: Objectives: Chemistry is the central science. By studying chemistry one can find answers of many questions that arise to an inquisitive mind. This course is to be offered to students who are curious and interested to know the realities of the world in terms of atoms, molecules, materials and their chemical reactions. Further, some light will also be thrown on the chemistry of some materials that we come across in our everyday life. 1. Basic Principles of Chemistry: Atoms, molecules, and their electronic structures. Types of Chemical bonding. Basic concept of Hybridization. Energetics of bond formation, Types of intermolecular/intramolecular forces, and molecular association for the formation of materials. 10 2. Chemical Reactions: Thermodynamic basis of chemical changes. Enthalpy, entropy, and free energy change during a chemical reaction. Types of Chemical Reactions. The concept of oxidation number, Reducing and oxidizing agents. 10 3. Applications of Chemistry in daily life : a) Dyes and pigments: General idea about the chemistry of dyes, Classification of dyes, Origin of the colors in the dyes and pigments, and application in garment and printing industries. b) Polymers: Natural and synthetic polymers, synthesis, properties, and applications. (Examples: polyester, rubber, nylon, bakelite, etc). Introduction to biopolymers. Application of synthetic polymers in surgical treatments and transplantations. c) Food and beverage industry: use of preservatives, food adulteration, flavor enhancers, artificial sweetening agents, and antioxidants. d) Fragrance: Basic principles, types of fragrances, and their applications. e) Cleansing agents: Soaps, detergents, Surfactants, and underlying chemistry of cleansing agents. 25 149 4. Reduction using metal hydrides

Objectives: To understand the wave nature of matter and its implications. To study the classification of elements and their properties. To study the states of matter; behavior of ideal and real gases, liquids, and the structures of solids.To understand the laws of thermodynamics. 1.Atomic Structure: Wave-particle duality, Heisenberg uncertainty principle, Schrodinger wave equation, Eigen values and Eigen functions, significance of Ψ and Ψ2 Radial and angular wave functions, Multi-electron system: Concept of Effective Nuclear Charge (Slater’s rules). 5 2. Atomic properties and their periodic trends: A brief introduction to the modern periodic table (Block wise). Atomic size (Covalent, Ionic and van der Waal’s radii; Lanthanide contraction), Electron loss, and electron gain enthalpies. Inert pair effect. Electronegativity (Pauling, Mulliken, Allred Rochow’s methods of determination): As a criterion of bond type. Lattice energy and its determination: a) Born-Haber cycle b) Born Lande equation c) Comparison of experimental and theoretical values. Solvation/Hydration energy (Solubility of ionic solids in water). Covalency in ionic compounds (Fajan’s rules). Redox reaction, Standard electrode potential and its determination. Electrochemical series and its applications Latimer and Frost diagrams; specific illustrative examples. 10 3. Gaseous State: Kinetic theory of gases and ideal gas laws, Maxwell distribution of speed, Equipartition of Energy collisions in a gas: collision number, collision diameter and mean free path, behaviour of real gases: van der Waals equation and its applicability, the critical state: critical constants, law of corresponding states. 10 4. Liquid State: Surface tension, capillary action, measurement of surface tension, viscosity of liquids and its measurement, temperature effect on surface tension and viscosity 4 5. Solid State: Crystal lattices, space lattice, unit cell, crystal systems, law of rational indices, Miller indices, Bragg’s equation, crystal structure of NaCl, graphite and diamond 4 6. Chemical Thermodynamics and its Applications: First law of Thermodynamics, Thermodynamic quantities (w, q, ∆U and ∆H) for isothermal and adiabatic reversible expansion of ideal gases, Kirchoff's relations, Joule effect, Joule-Thomson effect, Joule- Thomson coefficient of real (van der Waals) gases. Second Law of Thermodynamics, Carnot cycle, concept of entropy and its physical significance, entropy changes for an ideal gas, entropy changes at constant pressure and volume, entropy change in spontaneous processes, free energy and maximum work functions, conditions for spontaneous changes and equilibrium, Gibbs-Helmholtz equation, Maxwell relations. Statement of third law of Thermodynamics. 12 105

Objectives: To train the students with the quality control practices being adopted in the chemical and pharmaceutical industries. The course includes the principles related to statistical handling of data; quality control principles applicable in the laboratories as well as quality management systems including those laid down by the International Standard Organization (ISO). 1. Statistical Quality Control Techniques: Statistical treatment of data, Control charts, Performance Evaluation uncertainties in measurement, Validation of analytical methods, Elements of quality Assurance, Principles of Good Laboratory Practices, Good manufacturing Practices in Drugs and Pharmaceutical Industries, Accreditation of QC laboratories, Tools and Mechanisms ICHGuidelines on Drug substances and Products. 25 2. Quality Management and Standards: Quality Management System(QMS), Quality management concepts and principles: ISO 9001:2000 QMS, Case studies on ISO 9001: 2000 in chemical industries. ISO 14000 Series of Standards. Total Quality Management (TQM) in Chemical Industry. Six Sigma Approach to Quality: Applying Six Sigma to chemical Industries. 20

Objectives: Chemistry is the central science. By studying chemistry one can find answers of many questions that arise to an inquisitive mind. This course is to be offered to the students who are curious and interested to know realities of the world in terms of energy and its utilization. How solar energy is used by the plants and how we can manage various energy sources. Further, some light will also be shed on the importance of metals and chemistry of metal extraction. 1. Photosynthesis: Introduction- a key process for life on earth, Light reaction, Dark reaction, Factors affecting photosynthesis, Photorespiration, artificial photosynthesis. 2. Energy Sources and storage: Introduction to renewable (green) and non-renewable sources of energy. Requirement and consumption of energy in India. Worldwide potential of these sources. 8 Understanding (i) Definition (ii) source (iii) advantages/disadvantages (iv) environmental aspects (v) future scope/sustainability along with specific attributes of each of the following types: Non-Renewable: a) Thermal-Oil, natural gas, and coal Oil - Origin, composition, specification, and characteristics of petroleum products Natural gas - Classification (natural and synthetic gas), Natural gas reserves - India and World Coal: Coal reserves- India and World, Origin, composition, Action of heat on coal, Coal derived chemicals Nuclear energy - Radioactivity, Different types of radiation, Nuclear fission, Basic components of Nuclear power reactor. Renewable: a) Solar energy - Importance, storage, applications (solar cooker, solar weather heater, solar greenhouses, solar cell, absorption air conditioning) b) Biomass energy - biomass conversion, biogas generation (types of plants needed, plant wastes, materials), Utilisation of biogas, energy farming (biomass production for energy) c) Fuel Cell Li-ion battery 27 3. Objectives: To develop the skills of Chemical Analysis using sophisticated modern equipments to the students Using sophisticated Instruments in Chemical analysis and Characterization. This will enable them to understand the functioning of the equipment and their proper handling for qualitative and quantitative analysis of molecules and materials. 1. Thermoanalytical methods: Thermoanalytical methods: thermogravimetry, factors affecting thermogravimetric curves, derivative thermogravimetry (DTG), thermobalance. Applications of thermogravimetry, differential thermal analysis (DTA), factors affecting DTA curves, instrumentation, and application of DTA. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), theory, instrumentation, applications of DSC, thermometric titrations, and principal classification. 15 2. Electrochemical Analysis: Potentiometry – fundamentals, reference electrodes (hydrogen, calomel, silver, and silver chloride electrode).Indicator and ion selective electrode, instrumentation and measurement of cell and emf- conductance and conductometric titrations. 15 3. Structure Analysis: Diffraction Techniques: Elementary theory (Neutron. Electron and X-ray diffraction), instrumentation, and applications of X-ray methods (emission, absorption, diffraction, and fluorescence methods). Spectroscopic Techniques: Atomic absorption, Spectroscopy, Atomic emission spectrometry, UV-visible molecular absorption spectrometry, Molecular luminescencespectroscopy (fluorescence, phosphorescence, chemiluminescence). 15 148

Objectives: Sustainable development is one of the most important challenges to the human civilization today. Indiscriminate use of natural resources, such as fossil fuels has polluted not only the air, soil and water bodies near to us but also has damaged the outer atmosphere. This course will throw light on various aspects of environmental chemistry, Pollution and its causes and also potential remedies with an idea of sustainable development. 1. Introduction: Concept and scope of environmental chemistry, Pollution versus contamination, Receptor, Sink, and pathways of a pollutant. Terminology (DO, BOD, COD, TLV) used in environmental analysis and their estimation. 7 2. Environmental Segments: Atmosphere- Regions of atmosphere, Carbon Footprint, Greenhouse effect, and Global warming, ozone hole. Hydrosphere- Microorganisms in aquatic chemical reactions, eutrophication versus oligotrophication. Lithosphere- Soil profile, soil properties, organic and inorganic components of soil, micro- and macro-nutrients Biosphere. 22 3. Natural cycles of the environment: Hydrological cycle, oxygen cycle, nitrogen cycle, phosphate cycle, and sulfur cycle. 6 4. Pollution: Sources of air pollution, Auto exhaust emission, and its prevention. Air quality parameters, ELNino phenomenon, Water pollution, Acid rains, Waste–water treatment: domestic and industrial effluents. Water quality parameters. Objectives: To impart a comprehensive understanding of the chemistry involving carbonyl compounds, ylides, aromaticity, their reactivity patterns, and notable reactions in organic chemistry. 1. Chemistry of Carbonyl compounds: Preparations and reactions - addition and condensation reactions, Cannizzaro, Perkin, Aldol, Benzoin, Haloform, Mannich, and Baylis-Hillman reaction. Important reactions of acids, HVZ reaction, relative reactivity of acid chlorides, acid anhydrides, amides, and esters. 8 2. Chemistry of Phosphorous and Sulphur Ylides: Preparation and Reactions. Wittig reaction, Arbuzov rearrangement, Horner- Woodsworth Emons Modification 5 3. Aromaticity: A general concept of aromaticity antiaromaticity and homoaromaticity. Molecular orbital picture of benzene.Benzenoid and non-benzenoid systems, alternant and nonalternant hydrocarbons. 7 4. Aromatic Electrophilic Substitution: Mechanism of nitration, halogenation, sulphonation, and Friedel-Crafts (alkylation and acylation) reactions. Effects of substituents on ortho/para ratio, orientation and reactivity. 6 5. Preparation and Reactions of Phenols. 4 108

Objectives: To impart the knowledge of electrochemisty and electrochemical cells. They will also learn about various types of equilibria. 1. Electrochemistry: Arrhenius theory of electrolytic dissociation; Conductance of electrolytes in solution; Ionic conductance, transference number, Determination of transport number by moving boundary method. Kohlrausch's law of independent migration of ions, ion conductance and ionic mobility,applications of conductance measurements, conductometric titrations. 6 2. Chemical Cells and Electromotive Force: Types of Electrodes and electrode reactions, Electrode potential, Standard Electrode potentials, Electrochemical cells, EMF and chemical cell reactions. Free energy, enthalpy and entropy changes of cell reactions; Concentration cells with and without liquid junction, liquid junction potential, salt bridges, applications of EMF measurements.Glass electrode and determination of pH of a solution. Potentiometric titrations: acid-base and redox. Buffer Solutions, Acid- base Indicators 10 3. Phase Equilibria: Thermodynamics of phase transition, Clapeyron-Clausius equation, phase rule, phase diagrams of one-component (water) and two components (phenol-water and Pb-Ag) systems, distribution law, application to cases for dissociation andassociation, determination of equilibrium constant (KI + I2 = KI3). 8 4. Chemical Kinetics: Rate laws for zero, first, and second and Pseudo first-order reactions, steady state approximation, temperature dependence of rates of chemical reactions, Collision theory, qualitative concepts of transition state theory. 6 109
